info.title: DockPanel Mail API
info.description:
Send and manage mail on a DockPanel host over REST.

Messages are injected through Postfix's local `sendmail` wrapper, so they are DKIM-signed and delivered on exactly the same path as mail sent from the webmail, and a copy is filed into the sender's **Sent** folder.

## Authentication

Every route except `GET /health` requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Two kinds of token are accepted, and only one of them is a *mailbox*:

* **A mailbox token** — minted per-mailbox in Roundcube under **Settings → Mail API**. It may send as its own address and manage only its own mailbox (the `/v1/me/*` routes). This is the token an application should hold.
* **A panel API key** — one beginning with `dp_`, created in the panel under **Settings → API keys**. It is not bound to a mailbox; it authenticates as the panel does, which is what the server-wide `/v1/domains/*` and `/v1/queue/*` routes require.

The two are not interchangeable: a mailbox token gets `403` on a management route, a `dp_` key is refused by nothing but the panel's own authorization — and `GET /v1/me` reports which level the presented token is at, as `admin`.

get.summary: List, search and sort the messages in a folder
get.description:
`Drafts`, `Sent` and `Trash` are folders rather than routes: name one with `folder` and this is how it is read.

The listing carries the search the bundled Webmail offers. `q` is free text, and it understands the tokens a Roundcube user types into the search box (`from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `cc:`, `bcc:`, `body:`, `text:`, `reply-to:`, `followup-to:`, `is:`, `larger:`, `smaller:`, `since:`, `before:`, `older_than:`, `newer_than:`, `has:attachment`, `OR`, and a leading `-` to negate) as well as plain words, which are matched across the fields `search` names (`subject` and `from` by default — `subject` and `to` in `Sent` and `Drafts`). `filter`, `read` and `interval` expose the Webmail's dropdowns directly.

`scope` widens the read past one folder — `sub` adds its children, `all` reads every folder — and then every message carries the `folder` its `uid` belongs to. `sort` picks the column (`date` by default, or `arrival`, `subject`, `from`, `to`, `fromto`, `cc`, `size`, `none`) and `order` the direction (`desc` by default; `fromto` resolves to `from` or `to`, and `none` is Dovecot's own `uid` order with `order` still applied). `limit` and `offset` page over that order.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Folder to read. Defaults to `INBOX`. A query parameter rather than a path segment because folder names legitimately contain `/`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text to search for, matched across the fields `search` names. The tokens of the Webmail's search box are understood here too: `from:alice`, `-to:bob`, `subject:"two words"`, `is:unread`, `is:flagged`, `larger:1M`, `smaller:500k`, `since:2024-01-01`, `older_than:1M`, `has:attachment`, and `OR` between two terms.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Comma-separated fields `q`'s plain words are matched in. One or more of `subject`, `from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `body`, `text`, `reply-to`, `followup-to`, or `all`. Defaults to the Webmail's own set: `subject` and `from`, or `subject` and `to` when `folder` is `Sent`, `Drafts` or one of their children.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Comma-separated flags to keep, the Webmail's filter dropdown. One or more of `all`, `unread`, `read`, `flagged`, `unflagged`, `answered`, `unanswered`, `deleted`, `undeleted`, `draft`, `undraft`, `attachment`, `priority-highest`, `priority-high`, `priority-normal`, `priority-low`, `priority-lowest`.

parameters.name: read
parameters.description: Keep only read (`true`) or unread (`false`) messages. The same as `filter=read` or `filter=unread`, for the one filter people reach for first.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Keep messages from an interval ending today, the Webmail's date dropdown. `1W`, `1M` or `1Y` for the last week, month or year, and the negated `-1W`, `-1M`, `-1Y` for anything older than that.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Which folders to read: `base` (default) is just `folder`, `sub` adds its subfolders, `all` reads every folder. With anything but `base` each message carries the `folder` its `uid` belongs to.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Column to sort by. `date` is the `Date:` header and `arrival` is when Dovecot received the message. `fromto` is the Webmail's smart column — `to` in `Sent`/`Drafts`, `from` everywhere else — and is reported resolved as `from` or `to`. `none` is Dovecot's own order — folder by folder, `uid` ascending — with `order` still applied, so `desc` reverts each folder.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to `desc`, newest or largest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most messages to return. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 500.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Messages to skip, over the sorted order.

post.summary: Append a message to a folder
post.description: Writes a message into a folder without sending it — how a draft is saved. It is built by the same code that `/v1/send` sends with, so it takes the same fields, except that no recipient is required. When the mailbox does not hand the message back, `uid` is `null` and any `flags` were not applied.

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: Message ordinal, as `GET /v1/me/messages` reports it.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Folder the message is in.

delete.description: A delete in mail is a move to `Trash`. `permanent=true` expunges instead, and a message already in `Trash` is expunged either way.

parameters.name: permanent
parameters.description: Expunge instead of moving to `Trash`.

200.description: The message was deleted — moved or expunged, as `moved_to` and `permanent` report.

moved_to.description: Set when the message was moved rather than expunged.

post.summary: Move a message to another folder
post.description: How a message is restored out of `Trash`, or filed into `Sent`.

post.summary: Set the flags on a message
post.description: The flags the mailbox holds afterwards are read back, not predicted: `\Recent` is Dovecot's to set. Only `\Seen`, `\Answered`, `\Flagged`, `\Draft` and `\Deleted` may be set, with or without the leading backslash.

200.description: The message's flags after the change.
How much was in `Trash` when it was emptied.

get.description: Contacts are Roundcube's own, so this reads the same table the Webmail does. `q` is free text matched against the searchable fields, `group` restricts to a group's members, and `sort`/`order`/`limit`/`offset` page over the result.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text, matched against name, email, organisation, notes and the rest.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only the members of this contact group.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Column to sort by.

put.description: Only the fields present in the body change; the rest are left as they were.

delete.description: A soft delete, as the Webmail does it: the row is flagged and hidden, not removed.

get.summary: Read a group and its members

200.description: The group, with its member ids.

put.description: The body's `contact_ids` becomes the group's whole membership. Every id must be a contact this mailbox owns.

200.description: The group, with its new members.

post.description: The first identity becomes the standard one, as does any created with `standard: true`.

delete.description: The last identity cannot be deleted — every mailbox needs one to send as.

get.description: The Webmail's preference blob, decoded into JSON. Keys are Roundcube's own (`language`, `timezone`, `pagesize`, `message_sort_col`, …).

put.description: A shallow merge: the keys in the body are set and everything else is left alone. A key with a JSON `null` value is removed.

200.description: The full preferences after the merge.

parameters.description: `1` for recipients collected from mail you sent, `2` for trusted senders.

bearerAuth.description: A per-mailbox token minted in Roundcube (Settings → Mail API), or a panel API key beginning with `dp_`. Both travel in the same `Authorization` header.

Email.name: email
Email.description: A full mailbox address inside that domain.

Forbidden.description: The token is valid but is not allowed to perform a server-wide operation.

NotFound.description: No such domain, mailbox, or alias.

Internal.description: The operation failed on the server.

Ok.description: A management call proxied to the panel. The panel's own body is returned; its shape is not restated here.

MessageRequest.description: The parts of a message a caller sets. One schema for both doors, because a message written into a folder is built by the same code that sends one — only the sending differs.

from.description: Sender. Defaults to the token's mailbox, and is refused if it names any other address. A display name (`Name <a@b.c>`) is allowed.

to.description: Primary recipients. Required when sending; a draft may have none.

bcc.description: Blind recipients. They receive the message but never appear in its headers.

html.description: HTML body. With `text` too, the message is sent as multipart/alternative.

SendRequest.description: A message to send. The one difference from `MessageRequest` is `to`: a message may be stored in a folder with no recipient, but it cannot be sent to nobody.

id.description: The message's `Message-ID`, useful as a handle to key on.

admin.description: Whether this token may use the server-wide `/v1/domains/*` and `/v1/queue/*` routes.

forward_to.description: An address to forward to. Omitted or `""` clears forwarding.

used_kb.description: Bytes in use, in KiB, summed over every folder.

quota_mb.description: The limit, from the panel. `null` when no limit is set.

MessageSummary.description: One message, as a listing shows it.

uid.description: Mailbox ordinal. Stable within a folder until the message is expunged.

flags.description: Dovecot's flags for the message, split into a list.

date.description: The `Date` header, as the message wrote it.

folder.description: The folder this message is in. Present in a listing, which may read more than one folder; the uid alone is not unique across folders.

sort.description: The column actually sorted by. `fromto` is reported as its resolved `from` or `to`; `none` means Dovecot's own `uid` order, with `order` applied.

text.description: The stored message as it is on disk, headers included.

folder.description: Folder the message is in now.

to.description: Folder to move it to. Both must already exist.

MessageAppend.description: A message written into a folder instead of being sent — how a draft is saved.

folder.description: Folder to write into. The mailbox must already have it, so a typo cannot create one.

flags.description: Flags to set on the stored message. `\Draft` is what makes a saved message a draft.

id.description: The `Message-ID` this server generated for the message.

uid.description: The uid the message was stored as, or `null` when the mailbox did not hand it back — in which case the flags could not be applied either.

add.description: Flags to set. The leading backslash is optional.

flags.description: The flags the mailbox holds after the change, read back rather than predicted.

catch_all.description: Address that receives mail for unknown mailboxes. `""` or null disables it.

email.description: Either the local part (`sales`) or a full address inside the domain.

Contact.description: One address-book entry, as Roundcube stores it.

groups.description: Ids of the groups this contact belongs to.

changed.description: When the row was last written.

ContactInput.description: A contact to write. Every field is optional; on update only the fields present change.

email.description: A single value or a list of them.

phone.description: A single value or a list of them.

mobile.description: A single value or a list of them.

members.description: How many contacts are in it.

Identity.description: A sender identity: the From name, address and signature the Webmail composes with.

CannedResponse.description: A canned response the Webmail can insert into a message.

preferences.description: Roundcube's own preference keys and their values.

PreferencesInput.description: Preference keys to set (or remove, with `null`).

type.description: `1` recipient of sent mail, `2` trusted sender.
